notes: B3 unit (gendn-g8o), 2026-10-07: the page carried zero id attributes, so eight existing section headings gained ids on the heading element (#at-a-glance, #why-it-exists, #text-box-shorthand, #text-box-trim, #text-box-edge, #example-coloured-box, #example-icon-alignment, #browser-support) and NOTHING else in the page changed - no rewording, restructuring, added prose, or styling. The syntax id sits on the <h3> 'text-box (shorthand)' rather than the <h2> 'the properties' because that h2's fragment would be empty (it opens immediately with an h3). SOURCES RE-FETCHED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-07): the css-inline-3 editor's draft propdefs read text-box 'normal | <'text-box-trim'> || <'text-box-edge'>' (Applies to: block containers, multi-column containers, and inline boxes; Inherited: no; Initial: normal), text-box-trim 'none | trim-start | trim-end | trim-both' (Inherited: no), text-box-edge 'auto | <text-edge>' (Inherited: yes - matching the page's 'text-box-edge is separately inherited'); the draft's shorthand text reads 'omitting the text-box-trim value sets it to trim-both (not the initial value), while omitting the text-box-edge value sets it to auto (the initial value)', and its auto definition reads 'auto keyword uses the value of line-fit-edge, interpreting leading (the initial value) as text' - all consistent with the page. CARRIED DISAGREEMENTS, BOTH SIDES, NEITHER ADJUDICATED (the implementer owns the disclosure sentence and its pin): (1) Chrome milestone - the page's #at-a-glance and #browser-support read 'Chrome 149 (desktop + Android)' / 'Chrome 149+', while the ChromeStatus record (API, fetched 2026-10-07, accurate_as_of 2025-02-14) reads status 'Enabled by default' with desktop/android/webview milestone 133 and is_released true; the two agree on enabled-by-default, flag false, and desktop+Android coverage. (2) Firefox - the page reads 'No signal yet', the record's ff view reads 'Positive' (mozilla/standards-positions#1105). (3) Safari - the page reads 'No signal yet', the record's safari view reads 'In development' with the note 'Available under a flag, original bug https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=245599' (WebKit/standards-positions#432). (4) text-box-edge grammar - the page lists the keywords as flat single values (auto, text, cap, ex, alphabetic, ideographic, ideographic-ink) with one-direction descriptions, while the spec's production is <text-edge> = [ text | ideographic | ideographic-ink ] | [ text | ideographic | ideographic-ink | cap | ex ] [ text | ideographic | ideographic-ink | alphabetic ] - two positional values where cap/ex may only be the over edge and alphabetic only the under edge, and a single keyword assigns both edges where possible else defaults the missing one to text; the page's per-keyword direction descriptions are consistent with those constraints but the two-value grammar and positional limits are not shown. (5) Shorthand grammar spelling - the page prints 'normal | <text-box-trim> || <text-box-edge>' without the spec's property-reference quotes (<'text-box-trim'>) - cosmetic. (6) Fragment drift - the page's at-a-glance Spec link targets #text-box, an anchor that does not exist in the current editor's draft (HTTP 200, but the shorthand section is anchored #text-box-shorthand); the two propdef-trim/edge links do resolve. The page's 'Edge 149+ (tracking Chromium)' row is an inference; the ChromeStatus record carries no Edge data either way.
